description: Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken is a beloved dish featuring crispy fried chicken coated in a sweet, spicy, and tangy gochujang-based sauce. This popular Korean street food and late-night snack offers an irresistible crunch followed by a burst of savory flavors. Perfect for sharing, it's a true culinary delight that captures the essence of Korean comfort food.

instructions.title: Prepare and Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces. In a bowl, combine the chicken with salt, black pepper, 1 tsp grated ginger, garlic powder, and mirin. Mix well to coat and let it marinate at room temperature for 15-20 minutes while you prepare other ingredients.

instructions.title: Prepare the Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, potato starch, and baking powder. Gradually add the cold water, mixing until a smooth, pancake-like batter forms. Ensure there are no lumps. The batter should be thick enough to cling to the chicken.

instructions.title: First Fry the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot or deep fryer to 325°F (160°C). Dip each marinated chicken piece into the batter, ensuring it's fully coated, then carefully drop into the hot oil. Fry in batches for 5-7 minutes until lightly golden and cooked through. Remove the chicken and place on a wire rack to drain excess oil.

instructions.title: Prepare the Yangnyeom Sauce
instructions.text: While the chicken is frying, prepare the sauce. In a saucepan, combine gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, corn syrup, minced garlic, 1 tsp grated ginger, and sesame oil. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly until the sugar dissolves and the sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes. Set aside.

instructions.title: Second Fry for Crispy Texture
instructions.text: Increase the oil temperature to 350°F (175°C). Return the partially fried chicken to the hot oil for a second fry. Fry in batches for another 3-4 minutes, or until the chicken is deep golden brown and extra crispy. This double-frying technique is crucial for achieving the signature Korean fried chicken crispiness. Remove and drain on a wire rack.

instructions.title: Coat the Chicken with Sauce
instructions.text: Once all the chicken is double-fried, transfer it to a large bowl. Pour the warm Yangnyeom sauce over the chicken. Gently toss the chicken using tongs or a spatula until each piece is evenly coated with the delicious sauce. Work quickly to ensure the chicken remains crispy.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Transfer the coated Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken to a serving platter. Garnish generously with toasted sesame seeds and chopped green onions. Serve immediately as a delightful appetizer, snack, or main course with a side of pickled radish or rice. Enjoy!

tips: For ultimate crispiness, always double-fry your chicken. The first fry cooks the chicken, and the second fry at a higher temperature creates that irresistible crunch.
The quality of your gochujang greatly impacts the sauce flavor. Use a reputable Korean brand. If you don't have corn syrup, honey is an excellent substitute for sweetness and shine.
Serve Yangnyeom chicken immediately after coating to enjoy its crispy texture. It pairs wonderfully with a side of refreshing pickled radishes (치킨무 - chikin-mu) to cut through the richness.
article:
Get ready to embark on a culinary journey that will revolutionize your perception of fried chicken. Forget everything you thought you knew about crispy, juicy chicken, because Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken is here to set a new standard. This isn't just a meal; it's an experience, a symphony of textures and flavors that has captivated palates worldwide. From the bustling streets of Seoul to your very own kitchen, this iconic dish promises an unforgettable crunch followed by a luscious, sweet, spicy, and savory glaze. Its immense popularity stems from a meticulous frying technique that yields an impossibly thin and crisp crust, perfectly complementing the tender meat within. Then comes the star – the vibrant, glossy sauce that coats each piece, delivering a complex flavor profile that keeps you coming back for more. If you've been searching for the ultimate fried chicken recipe, your quest ends here.

## What is Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken?

At its heart, Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken is a beloved variety of Korean Fried Chicken (KFC), distinguished by its signature sticky, sweet, and spicy red sauce. The term "Yangnyeom" literally translates to "seasoned sauce" in Korean, perfectly describing the rich glaze that transforms ordinary fried chicken into a culinary masterpiece. Unlike its American counterpart, which often features a thick, breaded crust, Korean fried chicken boasts a delicate, almost translucent skin that shatters upon impact, thanks to a unique double-frying method and the use of starches like potato starch or cornstarch. This results in an incredibly light yet resilient crispiness that stands up beautifully to the sauce.

The Yangnyeom sauce itself is a complex blend of gochujang (Korean chili paste), gochugaru (Korean chili powder), soy sauce, garlic, ginger, rice vinegar, and a sweetener like sugar or honey. Some variations might include ketchup for a tangier note, or even a touch of cola for added depth and glossiness. The magic lies in the balance – a harmonious interplay of fiery heat, comforting sweetness, umami depth, and a subtle tang, all coating every nook and cranny of the perfectly fried chicken. It’s this irresistible sauce, combined with the unparalleled crispiness, that makes Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken a truly addictive dish.

## Ingredients You Need

To create your own batch of incredible Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken, gather the following ingredients:

For the Chicken:
*   2 lbs chicken wings or boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
*   1 tablespoon soy sauce
*   1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
*   1 teaspoon minced garlic
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper

For the Dredging Mixture:
*   1 cup potato starch (preferred for crispiness) or cornstarch
*   1/2 cup all-purpose flour
*   1 teaspoon baking powder
*   1/2 teaspoon salt

For the Yangnyeom Sauce:
*   1/4 cup gochujang (Korean chili paste)
*   2 tablespoons gochugaru (Korean chili powder, adjust to taste for spice)
*   2 tablespoons soy sauce
*   2 tablespoons rice vinegar
*   2 tablespoons sugar or honey
*   1 tablespoon minced garlic
*   1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
*   1 tablespoon sesame oil
*   2 tablespoons water (or chicken broth for richer flavor)
*   Optional: 1 tablespoon ketchup for tang, or 1 tablespoon corn syrup for extra gloss

For Frying:
*   4-6 cups neutral oil with a high smoke point (vegetable, canola, peanut)

For Garnish (Optional):
*   Toasted sesame seeds
*   Chopped roasted peanuts
*   Thinly sliced scallions

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Creating perfect Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken involves a few distinct stages, but each step is straightforward and crucial for the ultimate result.

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Pat the chicken pieces thoroughly dry with paper towels. This is vital for crispy skin. In a bowl, combine the chicken with soy sauce, grated ginger, minced garlic, sesame oil, and black pepper. Toss to coat evenly and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.

2.  **Make the Dredging Mixture:** In a shallow dish or a large zip-top bag, whisk together the potato starch (or cornstarch), all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt.

3.  **Prepare the Yangnyeom Sauce:** In a small saucepan, combine all the sauce ingredients: gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar (or honey), minced garlic, grated ginger, sesame oil, and water. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, stirring constantly until the sugar dissolves and the sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.

4.  **First Fry:** Pour the frying oil into a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, ensuring it's at least 3 inches deep. Heat the oil to 325°F (160°C). While the oil heats, dredge the marinated chicken pieces in the starch mixture, shaking off any excess. Fry the chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot. Fry each batch for 6-8 minutes, until lightly golden and cooked through. Remove the chicken with a slotted spoon and place it on a wire rack set over a baking sheet to drain. Let the chicken rest for at least 10-15 minutes. This resting period is critical for the double-frying technique.

5.  **Second Fry:** Increase the oil temperature to 375°F (190°C). Return the rested chicken to the hot oil in batches. Fry for another 3-5 minutes, or until the chicken is deeply golden brown and incredibly crispy. This second fry is what gives Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken its signature shatteringly crisp texture. Remove the chicken and place it on a clean wire rack.

6.  **Sauce and Serve:** Immediately after the second fry, while the chicken is still hot, transfer the crispy pieces to a large bowl. Pour the prepared Yangnyeom sauce over the chicken and toss gently but quickly to coat every piece evenly. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds, chopped peanuts, and sliced scallions, if desired. Serve immediately.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving truly exceptional Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken goes beyond just following the steps. Here are some expert tips to elevate your homemade version:

*   **Double Frying is Non-Negotiable:** This is the secret to the legendary crispiness of Korean fried chicken. The first fry cooks the chicken through and renders some fat, while the second, higher-temperature fry crisps up the exterior, creating that irresistible shatter-crisp texture. Don't skip the resting period between fries!
*   **Use Potato Starch:** While cornstarch works, potato starch creates a lighter, crispier coating that holds up better to the sauce. It's a game-changer for authentic Korean fried chicken texture.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Pot:** Frying too many pieces at once will drop the oil temperature, leading to soggy chicken. Fry in small batches to maintain a consistent oil temperature and ensure even cooking and crisping.
*   **Pat Chicken Dry:** Excess moisture on the chicken skin will steam rather than fry, preventing that desired crispiness. A very dry surface allows for better adhesion of the starch coating and a superior crunch.
*   **Balance the Sauce:** Taste your Yangnyeom sauce before tossing. Adjust the spice level with more gochugaru, sweetness with more sugar/honey, or tang with more rice vinegar. The perfect balance is key to the dish's appeal.
*   **Serve Immediately:** While the double-fried crust is remarkably resilient, Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken is best enjoyed fresh off the stove, when the chicken is piping hot and the sauce is glossy and clinging perfectly.

## Serving Suggestions

Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken is a star in its own right, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Korean accompaniments. The most classic pairing is with *mu sam* (pickled radish), whose tangy, refreshing crunch provides a perfect counterpoint to the rich, spicy chicken. A simple side of steamed white rice can help soak up any extra sauce and balance the flavors. For a complete Korean fried chicken experience, known as "chimaek" (chicken and maekju/beer), serve it alongside a cold lager or a light ale. Coleslaw or a simple green salad can also offer a refreshing contrast.

## Variations and Substitutions

The beauty of Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken lies in its adaptability. Don't be afraid to experiment:

*   **Spice Level:** Easily adjust the heat by increasing or decreasing the amount of gochugaru in the sauce. For a milder version, omit the gochugaru entirely.
*   **Sweetener:** Honey can be used instead of sugar for a more complex sweetness. Corn syrup or even a touch of brown sugar can also work, affecting the gloss and depth of flavor.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Substitute regular soy sauce with tamari and ensure your gochujang is gluten-free (most are, but check labels). Use a gluten-free all-purpose flour blend in the dredging mixture.
*   **Chicken Cut:** While wings and boneless thighs are popular, you can certainly use drumsticks or even a whole cut-up chicken. Adjust frying times accordingly.
*   **Air Fryer/Baked:** While the texture won't be identical to deep-fried, you can achieve a respectable crispiness by air-frying or baking the chicken. Air fry at 400°F (200°C) for 15-20 minutes, flipping halfway, then coat in sauce. For baking, preheat oven to 400°F (200°C), bake for 30-40 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and cooked through.

Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken is more than just a recipe; it's a testament to the vibrant and innovative world of Korean cuisine. With its irresistible crunch and perfectly balanced sweet and spicy sauce, it’s a dish that promises to delight your taste buds and leave you craving more. Follow these steps and tips, and you'll soon be enjoying your own masterpiece of Korean fried chicken right at home.
